articles.title: Ayush Doseja Scores Highest Run Total of Season, Falls Short of Century
articles.summary: Delhi's Ayush Doseja scored his highest run total of the season but fell short of a century against Bengal.
articles.content: Delhi's Ayush Doseja finally broke his duck on Tuesday, scoring his highest run total of the season but unfortunately falling short of a century in the process. The southpaw had endured a frustrating start to the 2026-27 domestic season, struggling to convert promising starts into substantial scores across both the Duleep Trophy and Ranji Trophy. Doseja's biggest challenge this season has not been a loss of form but rather converting opportunities into significant scores. He emphasized that he did not let outside pressure affect him, despite the scrutiny following his impressive 949-run season last year. In the early stages of the current season, Doseja had consistently started well, only to see his innings come to an abrupt end through unfortunate dismissals, including a run-out. His long-awaited big score came at a cost, as he was dismissed for 78 after being trapped down the leg side. Doseja reflected on his batting performance against Bengal, acknowledging that he was playing well despite getting out down the leg side. Delhi's score at the end of Day 2 stood at 299 for six, in response to Services' first innings total of 266. He expressed frustration over his previous dismissals, which had been largely due to unfortunate circumstances rather than poor batting. articles.title: Botox Users Report Decline in Treatment Efficacy
articles.summary: Some loyal Botox users claim the neurotoxin is not working as well as it used to, with typical treatments lasting between three to four months.
articles.content: Reports have surfaced from loyal Botox users claiming that the popular neurotoxin is not working as well as it used to. The typical duration of a Botox treatment is supposed to last between three to four months. However, some users are now questioning its effectiveness. Online forums and discussions reveal a range of theories behind this perceived decline in performance, from accusations of dilution by providers seeking more revenue to claims that users have developed immunity against the toxin. Conspiracy-level speculation has taken hold among Botox enthusiasts, with various explanations being proposed for the alleged decrease in efficacy. Dr. King emphasizes that it's crucial to pay attention to the quantity of Botox units administered rather than the concentration of saline solution used as a diluent. The number of units received is what determines how long the effects will last. According to Dr. King, 20 units remain 20 units regardless of whether they are delivered in a small or large volume of solution. This highlights one reason why Botox may not be lasting as long as desired by some patients. Another common issue contributing to shorter-lasting results is under-dosing, which Dr. King identifies as the primary concern. The effectiveness of Botox can vary significantly from person to person due to differences in muscle strength and biology. Some individuals metabolize Botox faster than others because their muscles are more powerful, which means that even if they receive the same dose as someone else, their treatment may not last as long. This variability is a key factor in determining how well Botox works for each individual, with some people experiencing its effects for three to four months and others seeing results for only two to three months. The reason behind these differences remains unclear, but it's essential to consider individual biology when evaluating the success of Botox treatments. The placement of Botox injections is also crucial in determining their effectiveness. Dr. King emphasizes that precise placement is vital, as improper injection techniques can significantly reduce the treatment's duration and efficacy. Visiting a reputable medical practice, such as a board-certified dermatologist or plastic surgeon's office, minimizes the risk of receiving counterfeit Botox or experiencing suboptimal results due to inexperienced practitioners. In contrast, seeking treatments from unlicensed professionals increases the likelihood of complications and reduces the chances of achieving satisfactory outcomes. While some patients may worry that repeated use of Botox will lead to reduced effectiveness or even complete resistance, Dr. King suggests this is not typically a concern for most individuals. In fact, many long-term patients find they can maintain their desired results with fewer units over time due to the muscle's gradual reduction in strength from repeated relaxation. New patients may notice movement returning sooner than those who have been receiving regular treatments, which could be attributed to the body's initial response to Botox. However, a small subset of patients does develop neutralizing antibodies against Botox, making treatments less effective. While Botox is effective for treating movement-related wrinkles, other treatments like lasers can be used to address skin tightening, pigmentation, texture, and wrinkles at rest. Dr. King emphasizes that these treatments are complementary rather than competitive, suggesting a modern approach to facial rejuvenation that is increasingly individualized and multimodal. articles.title: New York City Sandwich Tour Led by Expert Guide Ben Gollan
articles.summary: A group of 12 travelers, led by expert guide Ben Gollan, has embarked on a unique approach to exploring New York City's sandwich scene.
articles.content: A unique approach to exploring New York City has been taken by a group of 12 travelers, led by expert guide Ben Gollan. Known for his Instagram presence as A Man and His Sandwich, Gollan has spent nine years reviewing sandwiches across the city. Gollan's background is not typical of a food tour leader; he moved to New York from Australia in 2016 after working as a government lawyer. He had been running an Airbnb Experience that focused on sandwich reviews for almost as long. The idea was born out of his love for sandwiches, which began with a visit to Harry & Ida's, a former deli in the East Village. The tour starts with a dash across Bowery from a coffee shop in Cooper Square, where the group met. Gollan recounts how a pastrami sandwich at Harry & Ida's turned him into a professional sandwich enthusiast. He describes it as "a fourth-generation Jewish deli that broke every rule of pastrami sandwiches: it was thick-cut and fabulous." The East Village neighborhood is a key part of the tour, with its mix of past and present. The area's contrasts are still evident today, despite the passage of time. Gollan notes that his group is unusual in being mostly locals, rather than visitors. New York City's sandwich scene is incredibly diverse, reflecting the city's personality trait of diversity. From classic Italian deli subs to grab-and-go banh mi, there's no shortage of great options. As Gollan points out, sandwiches are economical, versatile and delicious, making them the perfect way to experience the city's culinary landscape. As we continue our culinary journey through New York City's diverse neighborhoods, we find ourselves in a tiny bottega on the Lower East Side, where traditional Roman cuisine meets modern twists on classic dishes. The shop, Via Della Scrofa, is a family-owned gem that imports Italian groceries and serves up authentic flavors in its small counter space. Its owner has managed to recreate the essence of Italy's culinary scene in this corner of New York City. Named after a Roman street, it's no surprise that the menu features dishes inspired by Italy's rich gastronomic heritage. The Porcodeddena panini, made with porchetta, is a popular choice among locals and visitors alike. But for our group, Gollan recommends trying something different - the Bono panini, which combines grilled eggplants, sun-dried tomatoes, arugula, and buffalo mozzarella in a warm rosetta roll. As we continue our culinary journey through New York's diverse neighborhoods, our guide shares stories about the local eateries we're visiting. One of these characters is Giovanni Bartocci, the owner of a restaurant that has become a hotspot for food enthusiasts. Gollan mentions that he isn't joining us for lunch, so I ask him why. He doesn't elaborate further, leaving me to wonder what his plans are. We head north on 1st Avenue and soon spot our next destination, Nishaan, marked by its bright cobalt-blue sign and stacks of rice bags outside the entrance. The line snaking out of this small space suggests that we're in for a treat. Nishaan's menu boasts an interesting fusion of flavors, with dishes like elote chaat and mango lassi, but it's their twist on the classic New York bodega staple - the chopped cheese - that has drawn a crowd. This desi take features a chapli kebab spiced up with peppers and onions, served with cilantro sauce and tamarind chutney. The restaurant's popularity is not surprising, given its origins as a pop-up at Smorgasburg and its subsequent win on season 18 of The Great Food Truck Race. Its unique blend of flavors has made it one of the most talked-about new restaurants in New York City since opening in August 2025. As we navigate through the crowded streets of New York City, our senses are overwhelmed by the sights and sounds of the Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade. The air is electric with excitement as dogs in elaborate costumes strut their stuff, drawing cheers from the enthusiastic crowds. To escape the chaos, we duck into an alleyway, where a tantalizing aroma wafts through the air, guiding us to our next destination. Our guide, Gollan, frantically scans his surroundings, exclaiming "We're taking a detour! as he leads us away from the throngs of revelers. Our destination is Sunny and Annie's, a no-frills neighborhood eatery that has been serving up classic sandwiches since 1997. With its reputation for being open 24/7, 365 days a year, it's a haven for those seeking a quick bite at any hour. The unassuming exterior belies the treasure trove of flavors waiting within. Upon entering Sunny and Annie's, we're greeted by a dazzling array of sandwich options, neatly listed on colorful sheets of paper stuck to the glass counter. With 92 handheld choices to explore, our eyes widen as we scan the menu, taking in names like the Jackie Chan, a bulgogi, cilantro, avocado, lettuce, jalapeños, and onions-filled roll, and the Australian, a chicken cutlet sandwich. As we peruse the menu, it's clear that Sunny and Annie's is not a place to linger over coffee or conversation. With so many options to try, we're eager to get started on our culinary journey through New York City's diverse neighborhoods, each one revealing its unique flavors and character. The East Village bar we're visiting has an unassuming entrance that belies its spacious interior and welcoming atmosphere. Couples on dates and families with young children are equally at home here, creating a lively yet relaxed vibe. Ben Gollan appears with our pho sandwiches, neatly wrapped in spinach tortillas. These unusual wraps smell like authentic Vietnamese pho and taste remarkably similar, but the addition of avocado throws off the traditional flavor profile. As we take our first bites, some members of our group opt for ciders or wine to accompany their meal. The conversation begins to wind back around to a question that's been plaguing us: what exactly constitutes a sandwich? Gollan seems eager to spark debate and encourages us to share our thoughts on the matter. Do hot dogs qualify as sandwiches? What about quesadillas or hamburgers? Can a pizza folded in half still be considered a sandwich? The more we discuss, the more contentious the issue becomes. Gollan teases us with tales of a famous 2006 Massachusetts lawsuit that shed light on this very question. In White City Shopping Center vs. Panera Bread, a judge ruled that a burrito is not, in fact, a sandwich. This decision allowed Mexican fast-casual joints to open near Panera Bread establishments without encroaching on the sandwich market. Gollan takes great delight in this ruling, joking that it's his Roman Empire". The point of this tour, he insists, wasn't to reach a definitive answer but rather to broaden our culinary horizons and challenge our assumptions. Gollan shares his own rules for what constitutes a sandwich: it must have a carb. This straightforward definition seems almost too simple in light of the lively debate we've just had. With so many variations on this theme, it's clear that there's no one-size-fits-all answer to this age-old question. The nuances of defining a sandwich are up for debate, but there's no denying the impact it can have on our understanding of New York City's culinary landscape. A key aspect of creating a satisfying sandwich is cooking its components separately, rather than simply placing them together in between two slices of bread. On this principle, Ben Gollan, Chief Sandwich Officer at A Man and His Sandwich, bases his approach to crafting the perfect sandwich on his NYC Sandwich Tour. articles.title: Slate Abandons Original Battery Plan for Electric Pickup
articles.summary: The company has switched to a single lithium-iron-phosphate battery pack from Gotion after initially planning to use a nickel-manganese-cobalt battery from SK On.
articles.content: Slate has made a significant change to its electric pickup's battery configuration. The company initially planned to use a nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) battery from SK On in the base model, but this is no longer the case. The original plan was for the base model to be powered by a 52.7kWh NMC battery with an estimated range of 150 miles. Those who opted for the upgraded version were supposed to receive an 84.3kWh pack that would provide around 240 miles of range. However, Slate has abandoned this plan in favor of a single lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) pack from Gotion, manufactured in Manteno, Illinois. This new battery configuration extends the truck's range to a projected 205 miles and helps maintain the company's advertised starting price of $24,950 (plus a $1,450 destination fee). It is worth noting that this estimate is based on an EPA test cycle and not a finalized EPA rating. Slate has confirmed that the base truck will use LFP batteries. The switch to LFP was likely influenced by changes in government policies regarding electric vehicles. The federal clean-vehicle tax credit had requirements for the origin of battery components and critical minerals, which made US-made NMC cells from SK On a more suitable choice than an LFP supply chain concentrated in China. The federal credit's elimination for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025, has removed one reason Slate had to design its truck around those sourcing requirements. The availability of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) batteries had improved significantly by 2025, allowing Slate to reconsider its sourcing requirements. According to Chris Barman, Slate's CEO, a supplier that was previously considered did not have the capacity needed and could not meet federal tax-credit rules restricting battery materials linked to certain China-linked entities. However, Gotion has now been able to produce LFP batteries in Illinois, approximately 90 miles from Slate's factory in Warsaw, Indiana. This is a significant improvement over the originally planned supply arrangement with SK On, which would have required transporting modules from Commerce, Georgia, some 710 miles away. The reduced logistics costs are a major advantage for Slate. The use of LFP batteries instead of NMC also offers cost savings due to their composition. Unlike NMC, which contains nickel, manganese, and cobalt in its cathode, LFP uses iron and phosphate. This makes LFP cheaper to produce while still providing a reliable source of power. Slate was eager to incorporate the new battery technology into its design, with Barman stating that it would enable the company to maintain its target price point while providing more range for customers. The new prismatic cells are also designed to stack directly into the battery pack, making better use of available space under the truck. The Slate Truck's switch to lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries has resulted in a lower overall cost for the vehicle. However, this decision comes with some compromises - LFP batteries store less energy per unit of size and weight compared to nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) batteries. The increased battery capacity from 52.7kWh to 65kWh, combined with aerodynamic and thermal improvements, has enabled a significant boost in range. The current Slate Truck now boasts an estimated 205 miles on a single charge, up from the original 150 miles. This increase in range is not solely due to the chemistry change. The power output of the vehicle has also been affected by the switch to LFP batteries, with the engine now producing 181 horsepower compared to the previously announced 201 horsepower. Despite this reduction, Slate still claims an 8-second 0-to-60-mph run. The battery and power train warranty for the truck remains at 10 years or 110,000 miles. articles.title: Sonos Introduces New Voice Assistant in Early Access on November 6
articles.summary: The company's new voice assistant will offer enhanced functionality and advanced capabilities, including natural language requests and broader general knowledge queries.
articles.content: Sonos is set to introduce its new voice assistant in early access on November 6, marking a significant development for the audio equipment manufacturer. This move comes as the company aims to revamp its software and features, following a previous app redesign debacle. The updated voice assistant will be part of an upcoming update rolling out this week, which includes various design tweaks and new features within Sonos' underlying software, dubbed Sonos 27. One of the key components of this software is the revamped voice assistant, designed to offer enhanced functionality. The original introduction of Sonos 27 in September highlighted its focus on third-party AI assistants like ChatGPT and custom agents. However, the new voice assistant brings a fresh approach by integrating more advanced features that allow for natural language requests and broader general knowledge queries. Sonos' new voice assistant, dubbed Sonos 27voice, can control playback on connected devices within your system, mirroring some of the capabilities seen in previous Voice Control features. It also offers basic functionality such as setting timers, interacting with smart home accessories, and providing current weather updates. In contrast to earlier iterations, Sonos 27voice boasts more advanced capabilities. According to the company's support page, it can comprehend complex queries and offer detailed answers on a wide range of topics, from music recommendations to sports news. The new voice assistant will reportedly be able to play specific albums or genres based on user requests, with the ability to target individual speakers or areas within your home. This level of functionality is reminiscent of modern AI assistants like the Google Assistant and Alexa integration offered by Sonos in previous models. To gain access to Sonos' new voice assistant, users will need to request early access through the Sonos app and receive approval from the company. This approach is likely a deliberate move by Sonos to test the feature with a smaller group of users before its full release in 2027. As part of this testing phase, Sonos aims to collect feedback from users and avoid any potential backlash that may arise from the introduction of the new voice assistant. The company has already faced criticism for its 2024 app redesign, suggesting that it is taking a cautious approach with the rollout of Sonos 27voice. In addition to the voice assistant feature, Sonos is also introducing two other new features: Presets and System Health. Presets allow users to save groupings of music and playback settings that can be instantly played from any Sonos device with a single tap. The new voice assistant from Sonos will initially be available in the US market alone during its early access phase, which starts on November 6. This rollout is limited to devices that support Sonos' S2 platform. Only English language support is included in this initial release of Sonos 27voice. articles.title: House of Representatives Control Hangs in Balance Ahead of Midterm Elections
articles.summary: Democrats seek to win a majority in the House, which would influence President Donald Trump's final two years in office.
articles.content: The fate of the House of Representatives hangs in the balance as Democrats seek to wrest control from Republicans, who have dominated the chamber for four years but now face significant electoral headwinds. A Democratic takeover would set a crucial tone and influence the direction of President Donald Trump's final two years in office, with party leaders vowing to launch aggressive investigations into his administration. This shift in power would also grant Democrats a key role in shaping major congressional actions, even if they don't have complete control over the legislative process. To win a majority, Democrats need to flip at least three seats and reach the 218 threshold required for control. In an effort to mitigate this risk, Republicans have spent the past year and a half redrawing congressional maps across the country in their favor. Historical trends indicate that the president's party typically suffers losses in midterm elections, which could be detrimental to Democrats' chances of gaining control of the House. Polls conducted ahead of Election Day revealed widespread voter discontent with Trump across various issues, including the economy and cost of living, further exacerbated by the ongoing Iran conflict and the administration's tariffs policy. These findings suggest that voters are critical of the president's handling of key concerns, which could translate into negative sentiment for Republican candidates. Despite these challenges, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has predicted a Democratic majority, although he has cautioned against expecting a landslide victory. In a recent campaign rally, Jeffries framed Election Day as "judgment day," underscoring the high stakes for both parties in this election cycle. In a significant shift in strategy, top Republican outside groups have withdrawn their support for several vulnerable House seats that were once considered competitive. This move has left millions of dollars in ad reservations unspent, which was initially intended to boost the campaigns of Reps. Mariannette Miller-Meeks of Iowa and other Republicans who represent battleground districts won by Trump in 2024. The abrupt change in strategy is a clear indication that the Republican Party is reassessing its priorities and redirecting resources to other areas where they believe they have a stronger chance of winning. The retirement of Republican Representative Don Bacon from his Nebraska district has significantly complicated the GOP's efforts to hold onto the seat. In a last-ditch attempt to protect their paper-thin majority, Democratic leaders have been crisscrossing the country, campaigning in key battleground districts that could make or break their chances of retaining control. This includes states like California, Texas, Florida, Ohio, Michigan, New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. As the stakes are raised, Republican candidates are warning voters about the perceived dangers of a Democratic takeover, with some accusing Democrats of promoting a radical agenda that would lead to an overreach of government power and undermine individual freedoms. articles.summary: The company is currently unsure when it will have sufficient stock to meet demand due to constrained supply.
articles.content: Apple's latest stock update has not been reassuring for customers eagerly anticipating the arrival of its foldable iPhone Duo in time for Black Friday and the holiday shopping season. The company is currently unsure when it will have sufficient stock to meet demand, with chief operating officer Sabih Khan stating that supply of the new device remains constrained. Apple's efforts to increase production are ongoing, but the exact timeline for achieving a balance between supply and demand remains uncertain. During an earnings call on Monday, Nov 2, Khan provided investors with an update on the iPhone Duo's stock situation, confirming that it was still difficult to predict when supply would catch up with current demand. The company is working hard to get the revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible. The iPhone Duo shortage has been a major concern for Apple since its official launch on Oct 23, when the device sold out shortly after hitting the market. According to reports, demand for the new smartphone has been nothing short of extraordinary, with Apple itself describing it as "smashing". Apple's inability to meet current demand is not the only challenge facing the company; rising memory chip costs driven by the AI industry have also emerged as a concern during recent earnings calls, highlighting broader issues affecting the tech sector. The iPhone Duo shortage is far from over, with shipping times extending well into 2027 for those who didn't manage to get their hands on one initially. This has led some carriers, such as Verizon, to offer gift cards as a gesture of goodwill to customers affected by the delays. Apple's partnership with Perryman, a titanium producer, is being deepened in an effort to meet demand for the iPhone Duo. This move was announced by Apple CEO John Ternus, who expressed enthusiasm for the early response from reviewers and customers to the device. Ternus emphasized that Apple is working hard to get the iPhone Duo into customers' hands as quickly as possible. However, despite these efforts, the company is facing a rare challenge in terms of supply chain management. The traditional reputation of Apple for a smooth supply chain has been disrupted by the high demand for the new device. The iPhone Duo shortage is not the only issue affecting Apple's operations, with rising memory chip costs driven by the AI industry also posing a significant concern. This has forced the company to increase prices on numerous products, although these decisions were made reluctantly, according to Apple executives. The recent price hike of Apple products has led some customers to explore alternative options. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 has seen a significant surge in sales, particularly following the release of the iPhone Duo. Sales figures indicate that the foldable smartphone saw a 20% increase in the week after the iPhone's launch. This trend is likely driven by concerns over Apple's reliability and durability. Reports of cracked displays on the iPhone Duo have added to the woes of potential buyers. As a result, some consumers may be opting for Samsung's innovative design instead. The combination of rising prices and technical issues has made it challenging for Apple to regain customer confidence. With many holiday shoppers already looking elsewhere, the company faces an uphill battle in terms of meeting demand for its latest products. articles.title: Apple Watch Update Brings Faster Music Recognition and Sound Alerts
articles.summary: A new beta version of Apple Watch introduces Audio Intelligence, a set of features that includes music recognition and sound alerts, which can be activated through the iPhone's Settings app.
articles.content: Apple Watch users are in for a change as a new beta version starts rolling out this week, bringing Siri capabilities to the Series 12 and Ultra 4 models. This update introduces Audio Intelligence, a set of features that includes music recognition and sound recognition. Music recognition has been available on Apple Watch since its launch, but it now works faster and more seamlessly than before. Users can identify songs without even opening the Shazam app, with the feature integrated directly into their watch's interface. Songs are automatically added to the Smart Stack for easy access. Audio Intelligence also includes a new Sound Recognition feature that alerts users who are deaf or hard of hearing to important sounds in their environment, such as a crying baby, barking dog, or doorbell ringing. This can be particularly helpful for individuals with hearing impairments. To enable these features on an Apple Watch, users must first activate them on their connected iPhone through the Settings app. Under Accessibility > Sound and Name Recognition, users can toggle the feature on and select which sounds they want it to identify. The Apple Watch's Siri feature has been successfully identifying various sounds in my testing, including a fake cough, doorbell and car horn. However, I encountered some inconsistencies where it incorrectly identified non-existent sounds such as barking dogs or honking cars, making me question its accuracy. Further testing is needed to fully assess the capabilities of this new feature, which may be affected by the beta versions I'm currently using. The feature's performance could vary depending on the specific software and hardware configurations. The Siri Rewind feature allows users to double-click the Digital Crown at any point during the day to access a text snippet of what was said in the previous 15 seconds. This feature is similar to Live Photos, which captures a few seconds of video before and after taking a photo. When accessing the transcribed text, it disappears if no action is taken after viewing it on screen. Users can either ask Siri about it or save it to the Siri app for later review on their phone. The old audio is continuously replaced by new audio and then deleted, so if the feature isn't triggered, the last 15 seconds of conversation will be lost. The new Apple Watch feature, Siri Recap, is designed to summarize conversations in real-time, allowing users to revisit key points without having to ask the speaker to repeat themselves. This could be particularly useful during situations like reviewing a restaurant menu after the waiter has left the table. Siri Recap can run in the background and generate high-level summaries of conversations throughout the day, covering a range of topics from work meetings to spontaneous discussions with colleagues or family members. The feature is not intended for recording entire conversations, but rather as a tool to quickly recall key points without having to ask others to repeat themselves. Users can access the notes generated by Siri Recap through the Siri app and export them to either the Notes or Journal app. If left unattended, these notes will automatically delete after seven days, although users have the option to manually delete them at any time. This feature is part of a suite of tools aimed at improving user convenience. Both Siri Recap and its companion feature, Siri Rewind, are opt-in features that require explicit setup during initial configuration for them to function properly. When Siri Recap is activated on your Apple Watch, you can choose how it functions in terms of timing. You have the option to leave it running continuously, allowing Siri to automatically identify and summarize important conversations. Alternatively, you can schedule it to run during specific periods, such as when you're attending important meetings. Additionally, you can activate it manually through a new icon located within the Control Center. If you opt for continuous operation, Siri Recap will periodically remind you to check your summaries throughout the day. Notifications will also be triggered when scheduled events begin or end, keeping you informed about its status. Furthermore, if you forget to turn off the feature, you'll receive a reminder in the morning to disable it. This ensures that you remain aware of what's happening with your Siri Recap. It's worth noting that both Siri Recap and its companion feature, Siri Rewind, are designed to work within specific limitations. For instance, they won't function during conference calls or FaceTime sessions if you're using AirPods or headphones connected to the Apple Watch. Instead, they'll only capture audio picked up through the watch's speaker. Apple has also addressed concerns about battery drain associated with these features. According to the company, running all four features continuously will not significantly impact your Apple Watch's battery life. In fact, the Apple Watch Series 12 can last for a day and a half on a single charge, while the Ultra model can run for up to three days without needing a recharge. The Apple Watch's new S11 chip is a significant improvement in terms of power efficiency and processing capabilities. This dual-architecture design allows for background tasks to be handled without draining the main processor's resources. The watch itself does not store audio recordings; instead, raw audio is processed within a secure compartment on the S11 chip called the Secure Exclave. Apple emphasizes that even it cannot access this isolated area, which adds an extra layer of protection. Siri Recap also takes steps to protect user data by condensing conversation transcripts before sending them to Private Cloud Compute. This condensed version excludes sensitive information such as financial data, authentication details, personal identifiers, and language related to self-harm or government secrets. Apple's approach to security and accessibility is centered around protecting users' privacy. The company presents a convincing case for its measures, which are designed to safeguard sensitive information while still providing useful features like Siri Recap. The ability of the Apple Watch to listen in on conversations raises concerns about privacy, particularly when others may not be aware that their discussions are being recorded. Unlike some smart glasses, there is no visible indicator on the watch when Siri is actively recording a conversation. Apple's latest addition to its Apple Watch is a feature that allows users to access Siri directly from their watch. This development has raised concerns about user privacy, as some critics argue that this integration could lead to uninvited listening and recording of conversations. The new feature will be available in English initially, with other languages to follow later. It will roll out in beta form with the update to iOS 27.3, giving users a chance to experience it firsthand before it becomes a standard feature. articles.title: Hidden Cameras Found in Short-Term Rentals
articles.summary: Short-term rentals like Airbnb have raised concerns about surveillance devices being used to spy on visitors.
articles.content: Traveling has become a worrisome experience for many due to the risk of hidden cameras in rental properties. Short-term rentals like Airbnb and hotels have raised concerns about surveillance devices being used to spy on visitors. The issue is particularly prevalent in privately owned rentals where owners can install recording devices without guests' knowledge. While some may argue that security cameras are a necessary feature, especially doorbell and outdoor cameras, indoor recording devices are strictly prohibited by hosting platforms like Airbnb. A 2024 report revealed the alarming number of support tickets related to surveillance devices processed by Airbnb in the past decade. Although the exact figure is not specified, it's clear that this issue has been ongoing for some time. The platform emphasizes its commitment to guests' safety and security by banning indoor recording devices from listed properties. Despite the relatively low incidence rate, with less than 0.1 percent of properties reported to have surveillance issues, many visitors remain skeptical about short-term rentals. According to recent statistics, a significant majority, around 51 percent, of travelers do not trust these types of accommodations due to legitimate concerns about hidden cameras and other security risks. As guests become increasingly aware of the potential risks, it's essential for them to take proactive steps in ensuring their safety. With cameras often disguised as ordinary household items like smoke detectors or picture frames, a quick check can help alleviate worries about being monitored. A flashlight sweep is an effective way to detect hidden cameras in a room. Begin by closing the curtains and turning off the lights, then use a flashlight to methodically scan the space for any signs of electronics that might indicate the presence of a camera. Common places where cameras are often concealed include smoke detectors, air purifiers, televisions, shower heads, or lights. Be especially vigilant when checking areas such as near the bed or in the shower, as these locations may pose significant privacy concerns. Shining a flashlight at mirrors can also help identify potential issues. A genuine mirror should reflect light in a way that allows it to bounce back, whereas a two-way mirror will make it appear as though there is no gap between your finger and its reflection when you place a finger directly on the surface. Night-vision cameras, which emit infrared light, can be detected using the camera app on your phone. This type of camera will typically produce purple or white dots on your screen. To verify whether your phone has this capability, try pointing it at a TV remote control and pressing the buttons; if the remote's LED lights are detectable through the camera, you should see some indication. Once you've confirmed that your phone can detect infrared light, use both its front-facing and rear cameras to scan the room for any signs of IR emissions. This may help identify potential night-vision cameras in the area. When scanning a network for hidden cameras using mobile apps like Fing, Net Analyzer or WiFiman, it's essential to recognize unfamiliar device names that may indicate recording devices are present. articles.title: SUSE to Lay Off Approximately One in Ten Employees Due to Impact of Automation and Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: The company will be laying off approximately one in ten employees from its global workforce of nearly 2,000 people as part of a broader effort to adapt SUSE's organizational design and cost structure to keep pace with rapidly advancing AI capabilities.
articles.content: SUSE, a leading provider of enterprise Linux solutions, is undergoing significant restructuring efforts in response to the growing impact of automation and artificial intelligence (AI) on its operations. According to an email sent by CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen to staff, the company will be laying off approximately one in ten employees from its global workforce of nearly 2,000 people. This decision is part of a broader effort to adapt SUSE's organizational design and cost structure to keep pace with rapidly advancing AI capabilities. Van Leeuwen acknowledged that AI is revolutionizing the way software companies operate, forcing them to rethink their approaches to work and productivity. He noted that the current business model and cost base will not be sufficient to support the company's future growth and success in an increasingly automated industry landscape. Staff affected by the layoffs will be notified by November 4, although specific details on which roles will be terminated have not been disclosed. The move highlights the growing impact of AI on various sectors within the tech industry, including open-source software development. Layoffs attributed to AI have become a growing trend in the tech industry, but it's not always clear whether human roles are being replaced or simply reorganized. Microsoft's recent decision to buy out 60,000 of its workers is a prime example of this blurred line. While some companies may be laying off employees due to AI's growing capabilities, others might be using AI as a convenient excuse for restructuring their workforce. Jobloss.ai's layoff tracker shows that tech giants like Uber and Salesforce have also been impacted by job losses attributed to AI. The difficulty in determining whether AI is truly responsible for layoffs or just being used as a scapegoat is further complicated by the fact that some companies may be over-investing in AI infrastructure. Squarespace's recent announcement of 19% staff cuts, for instance, does not explicitly mention AI as a reason, but it's worth noting that the company has invested heavily in AI offerings. The impact of AI on jobs is still being felt across various sectors, and its effects are not always immediately apparent. As companies continue to navigate this complex landscape, one thing is certain: the role of AI in shaping the future of work will only become more pronounced in the days to come. SUSE's recent layoffs have sparked debate about the impact of AI on the workforce, but experts warn that a massive wave of job losses is yet to come. As companies continue to adopt new technologies and streamline their operations, existing roles are becoming redundant, according to SUSE CEO Nils Braunschweig. He has acknowledged that modern tooling is changing daily workflows, allowing teams to work more efficiently with fewer overheads. However, economists argue that while AI may be replacing some jobs, it will also create new ones and companies will need to adapt their workforce planning strategies to stay ahead of the curve. In fact, research suggests that by 2029, many firms will rehire employees they initially replaced with AI at a higher cost. Ultimately, as companies navigate this complex landscape, one thing is certain: the role of AI in shaping the future of work will only become more pronounced in the days to come, driving significant changes in the way businesses operate. articles.summary: The average price of new smartphones is expected to increase by nearly 28 percent this year due to a global memory shortage.
articles.content: The cost of new smartphones continues to rise due to a global memory shortage, pushing forecasted average prices up by nearly 28 percent this year compared to last. Mobile carriers have introduced promotions to attract customers, offering discounts or free phones when switching providers. However, these deals often come with strings attached, and the true cost is hidden in fine print, such as expensive data plans or financing agreements. Replacing an old Android phone can be costly, with prices ranging from hundreds to over a thousand dollars for a new device. Before shelling out this kind of money, consider exploring low-cost solutions that can extend the life of your current smartphone. One common issue affecting older Android phones is battery degradation. A worn-out battery can slow down charging times and cause rapid power consumption, impacting overall performance and causing frustrating lag or freezing. Battery health plays a crucial role in a phone's ability to perform tasks efficiently. When batteries degrade, they cannot provide the quick bursts of power needed for processor-intensive activities, leading to sluggish loading speeds and system freezes. In many cases, simply replacing an aging battery can breathe new life into an old Android device, rather than discarding it for a costly upgrade. Replacing an aging battery can be a cost-effective solution for revitalizing older Android devices, rather than discarding them for expensive upgrades. Many phone users mistakenly attribute poor performance to the device itself and end up spending hundreds on new models. However, a fresh battery at a fraction of the price can breathe new life into their outdated smartphones. For those with phones that have removable backs, such as Samsung Galaxy models, replacement lithium-ion batteries are readily available on Amazon for between $10 and $20. For devices with sealed backs, users may need to invest in DIY repair kits or opt for professional battery replacement services. These options typically range from $60 to $80, significantly lower than the cost of purchasing a new phone. While these costs may seem substantial, they are still a more affordable alternative to upgrading to a brand-new device. In addition to replacing batteries, optimizing existing ones can also help extend their lifespan. Android devices often come equipped with battery-saving modes that reduce power consumption by limiting features such as screen brightness or disabling less frequently used apps. Some smartphones, like Google Pixel models, offer advanced battery optimization features. These include Adaptive Battery, which restricts the running time of infrequently used apps and learns user patterns to optimize battery life. Similar capabilities are also available on many Samsung phones, allowing users to put their less-used applications into sleep mode to conserve power. To make the most out of an older Android phone's battery life, it is crucial to keep its charge level within a specific range throughout the day. This means avoiding both extremely low and high levels of charge, as they can cause chemical stress on the battery. Research suggests that keeping the battery between 20 and 80 percent charged reduces exposure to this stress, resulting in a longer battery life. Specifically, it is estimated that doing so can extend the battery's lifespan by two to three times compared to charging it to 100 percent consistently. A simple yet effective solution for prolonging an older Android phone's overall lifespan is using a sturdy case and screen protector. While aesthetics may not be a priority when aiming to squeeze out as much life from an old device, these accessories can greatly improve the phone's durability and usability. Protecting the phone with a case and screen protector also reduces the likelihood of costly repairs or replacements due to accidental damage. In many cases, a solid case is inexpensive and can provide peace of mind for users who want to get the most out of their older Android device. Keeping an older Android phone updated with the latest operating system is essential for maintaining its security and functionality. This includes receiving critical security patches that address potential vulnerabilities to hackers, as well as ensuring compatibility with various apps on the device. Most updates also bring performance improvements and bug fixes, which can further enhance the overall user experience of an older Android phone. Users should prioritize keeping their devices up-to-date, especially when considering the significant benefits it offers in terms of security and app compatibility. Installing the latest updates can breathe new life into an old Android phone. However, it's essential to note that newer OS versions are optimized for newer phones with advanced components, which may lead to performance lag on older devices. Older phone processors and reduced memory capacity can struggle to keep up with the demands of updated operating systems, resulting in noticeable slowdowns. Despite this trade-off in performance, opting for the latest updates might be worth considering if it means extending the lifespan of your trusty old Android device. Ultimately, the reality is that phones are not built to last indefinitely and will eventually require replacement. By following these tips, however, you may be able to extract a bit more utility from your older Android phone before needing to invest in a new one. This season has seen Ty Jerome emerge as one of the league's top scorers, averaging an astonishing 28.3 points per game on remarkable shooting splits of 50/42/88. The question on everyone's lips is: what sparked Jerome's sudden rise to stardom? While it's true he was once a relatively unknown player, there were signs of potential that had been building over time. His consistent progress and growth as an NBA player have made this scoring boom somewhat predictable, despite its scale being anything but expected. Jerome's breakout season with the Cavaliers in 2024-25 marked a significant turning point in his career. Following years of being traded between several teams, including the Suns, Thunder, and Warriors, he found stability in Cleveland. His impressive performance earned him third place in Sixth Man of the Year voting. During the Cavs' first-round sweep over the Heat, Jerome averaged an astonishing 16 points per game, showcasing his scoring prowess. He made 10 out of 20 three-pointers and shot at a 51% overall clip, demonstrating his ability to perform under pressure. The Grizzlies' decision to sign Jerome to a three-year, $28 million contract in the summer of 2025 is looking like a shrewd move as he continues to make an impact on the court. Jerome's impressive scoring average has been a consistent trend throughout his career. In his Grizzlies debut, he scored 20 points in just 20 minutes of play, demonstrating his ability to produce even in limited opportunities. This season, Jerome is playing more minutes than ever before, and it's clear that his increased usage rate is contributing to his high scoring average. He is currently averaging 0.91 points per minute played, a mark that puts him among the league leaders in this category. As Jerome continues to play at an MVP level, it's worth noting that his scoring surge didn't come out of nowhere. His minutes and usage have increased steadily over time, and he has consistently shown himself to be a high-scoring threat whenever he takes the court. Liu is currently unwinding at his hotel before taking on the night's events, clad in a robe and sitting barefoot on the sofa with a metallic device in hand. He was swiping it across his face, revealing an unblemished complexion that glows in the light. Liu's grooming routine continues as he leans back into the chair, allowing Keating to work her magic on his hair. A room service trolley sits nearby, stocked with snacks and drinks that Liu can access at will. As a young adult from a working-class background, Liu admits that it took time for him to develop an appreciation for fashion. articles.title: Ireland Faces Challenges in Tourism Market Amid Economic Uncertainty
articles.summary: Tourism Ireland's Chief Executive Alice Mansergh highlighted the challenges facing the country's tourism market at the Skift Transatlantic Summit.
articles.content: A major challenge is emerging for Tourism Ireland as it navigates a rapidly changing travel market. The country's Chief Executive, Alice Mansergh, highlighted this issue at the Skift Transatlantic Summit, where she discussed the island of Ireland's strategies to maintain its appeal to travelers. North America remains one of Ireland's most valuable visitor markets, but the outlook is becoming increasingly uncertain. Despite continued growth in visitor numbers, there are signs that demand may be softening due to higher costs and economic uncertainty affecting travelers' spending habits. So far this year, Ireland has seen a 5% increase in visitors from North America, with these tourists also spending 10% more than previous years. However, the past few months have been marked by a slowdown in bookings as travelers become more cautious about their finances. In an effort to counteract this trend, Tourism Ireland is placing greater emphasis on its marketing strategy. The new "Ireland Goes Beyond" campaign aims to showcase the unique experiences and attractions that make Ireland an attractive destination for visitors. The campaign focuses on highlighting the country's natural beauty, rich culture, and heritage as well as offering authentic local experiences that can help keep it at the top of travelers' wishlists despite the current economic uncertainty. Maintaining air connectivity between Europe and North America is crucial for Ireland's tourism industry, according to Tourism Ireland. With jet fuel costs rising sharply and fewer Europeans traveling to the U.S., airlines are reassessing which transatlantic routes remain profitable. To mitigate this challenge, Tourism Ireland works closely with carriers to promote strategic routes and stimulate inbound demand. The agency aims to fill planes to keep flights running, as Mansergh succinctly put it. Healthy two-way travel is essential because weaker outbound traffic from Europe can put pressure on the same routes that bring North American visitors to Ireland. Weaker connectivity can be damaging for Ireland's tourism industry, according to Mansergh. The agency is therefore focused on maintaining air connections with key markets. North America accounts for just over a third of Ireland's inbound overseas revenue, while Europe contributes roughly another third. Britain offers another opportunity, with visitors from the nearest neighbor twice as likely to return. Tourism Ireland recognizes that diversifying its visitor base is crucial in this uncertain market. The agency acknowledges that relying too heavily on one market can be risky, and now is not the time for such dependence. To adapt to the evolving travel landscape, Tourism Ireland is revamping its digital strategy by leveraging generative AI. The organization's content now contributes to a significant portion of queries about the destination across popular AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. The goal is to shape the recommendations provided by these platforms, favoring lesser-known attractions and local businesses that might otherwise go unnoticed. This approach aims to showcase Ireland's unique experiences and cultural heritage. Tourism Ireland is also aware that visibility in AI search depends on online conversations about a destination. The organization has taken this into account when promoting Halloween as a celebration rooted in the ancient Irish festival of Samhain. To build awareness, Tourism Ireland has been sharing its own content across various platforms, including Reddit and YouTube, while also engaging with travelers on Tripadvisor. This multi-channel approach aims to create a cohesive message about what Ireland wants to be known for. The organization's focus is not solely on technology-driven experiences but also on authentic cultural encounters that bring visitors closer to local traditions. Examples of such experiences include sheepdog demonstrations, cider-making farms, and traditional currach-building. Tourism Ireland is prioritizing authenticity in its marketing efforts to cater to travelers' growing desire for real-life experiences. The organization's focus on digital connectivity will continue in 2027, as it aims to reach visitors through new channels and provide them with compelling reasons to visit the country. This approach reflects Tourism Ireland's strategy of protecting established connections while exploring emerging opportunities. By doing so, Tourism Ireland is giving travelers a strong incentive to explore more of the island of Ireland, which will ultimately drive tourism growth in the face of an increasingly uncertain market. articles.title: Disconnect Between Republican Voters' Priorities and Party Messaging Revealed
articles.summary: A new poll has shown that nearly half of all voters consider cost of living and affordability crucial issues in their decision-making process, but only 23% of Republican voters say the same about the party's priorities.
articles.content: A new poll has revealed a significant disconnect between what Republican voters want their party to focus on and what they say is actually being prioritized. The economy, specifically the cost of living, is the top concern for most Americans when it comes to voting decisions. According to the poll results, nearly half of all voters - 47% - consider cost of living and affordability as crucial issues in their decision-making process. This includes a significant proportion of Republican midterm voters, with 44% citing these concerns as among their top priorities. In contrast, when asked which issues are most important to the GOP, a plurality of Republican voters - 39% - named immigration and deportations as a top priority for the party. Only 23% said cost of living and affordability were a top concern for the party, highlighting a significant gap between what voters want their party to focus on and what they say is actually being prioritized. The economy and jobs ranked second in terms of voter concerns, but it appears that Republican voters are not seeing their party's priorities align with these issues. This disconnect may be a warning sign for the GOP as midterm elections draw near. A significant number of Republican voters feel that their party is not prioritizing economic issues as much as it should be. In recent speeches, former President Trump has tended to focus on other topics, such as cultural concerns and even the physical appearance of some GOP candidates, rather than the economy. This emphasis on non-economic matters may have a bearing on the party's messaging ahead of the midterms, especially given that many Americans are grappling with rising costs of living. Meanwhile, there is less dissonance among Democratic voters, who tend to prioritize economic issues like affordability and cost of living in their party's platform. Republican strategist Jeff Burton expressed concerns about the poll results, stating that they do not bode well for the party's prospects. Burton attributed the disconnect between GOP voters' economic concerns and the party's messaging to a failure to effectively communicate its stance on affordability and cost of living issues. A recent survey conducted by PF Global underscores this challenge, highlighting the difficulties Republican candidates have faced in conveying their economic policies to voters. Despite campaigns and outside groups spending over $800 million on ads focused on economic talking points, with Democratic-aligned groups allocating roughly $401 million and Republican-aligned groups allocating around $311 million according to AdImpact's tracking of TV ad data, the GOP has struggled to convince voters that it is addressing their economic concerns. Republican strategists point to one possible explanation for this disconnect: the influence of Trump, who some believe may be hindering the party's ability to effectively address economic issues. As election day approaches, some Republican strategists are pointing fingers at a key factor contributing to their party's struggles: Donald Trump's influence on the party's messaging. Longtime Arizona Republican strategist Chuck Coughlin expressed his frustration with Trump's campaign stops in Florida, South Carolina, and Ohio last week. The analysis of these speeches revealed that Trump spent only around 10% of his time discussing economic issues like prices and inflation. In stark contrast to this limited focus on the economy, Trump devoted more minutes to other topics such as advocating for a politician's resignation and addressing the ballot controversy in Alaska than he did to talking about affordability. This imbalance has left many wondering if Trump's narrative is hindering the party's ability to connect with voters on economic issues. The disconnect between what Republican voters care about and the party's messaging was highlighted by a recent poll, which found that GOP voters believe their party isn't focused enough on the economy. President Trump's White House has emphasized the administration's economic achievements in recent days, highlighting a significant tax relief package that has secured billions of dollars for individual taxpayers. This focus on taxes and other economic issues is at odds with the president's public statements and policy initiatives, which have often centered on cultural and social issues such as guns, transgender rights, and landmark renaming. Despite this disconnect, White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton pointed to a major tax relief package as evidence of the administration's commitment to supporting hardworking families. A recent poll has found that Republican midterm voters are more concerned with economic issues than those highlighted by President Trump in his public statements and policy initiatives. The poll results suggest that voters are looking for their party to focus on tangible, economic benefits rather than cultural or social issues. A significant majority of Republican midterm voters want their party to focus more on economic issues, with 64% calling for increased attention to the economy and cost of living. Immigration and border security also rank high, with 42% of respondents demanding more discussion. The prominence of economic concerns in this election cycle has relegated other issues, such as abortion rights and transgender issues, to secondary status.
